root_cause: huff_decode() mutates the caller's array-of-pointers argument (advancing data[0]/data[1] by one element in certain code paths) as an implementation detail to signal 'first element already consumed', but ec_pair_dec() was written assuming p_data[] always points at the base of the fixed-size data_pair[] arrays. Combined with an unconditional fixed iteration count (nb_bands) in attach_lsb(), the mismatch between the (possibly shifted) pointer and the full-length loop bound produces an out-of-bounds access.
findings: In ec_pair_dec(), p_data[0]/p_data[1] are initially set to point at the base of the fixed-size local arrays data_pair[0]/data_pair[1] (each int16_t[28]) and are then passed by reference (int16_t *data[2] decays to int16_t **) into huff_decode().
